question:
As it is used in the text, what does the word "consideration" most nearly mean? The passage below is adapted from Henry James's 1881 novel The Portrait of a Lady.
Every action Osmond took was a pose--a pose so cleverly measured that an unwary observer would mistake it for spontaneity. Ralph had never encountered anyone who dwelt so completely in the realm of consideration. His preferences, his studies, his talents, his collections--all of them served some deliberate aim.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Osmond's poses are so carefully measured that "consideration" here signals calculation.

question: According to the text, what term is used for a person whose profession is judging books? Natalie Babbitt's first published book, The Search for Delicious, appeared in 1969. A debut novel is an author's very first published book. Books like these hold special appeal for readers and for literary critics--the professionals whose job is to evaluate books--because they introduce fresh voices to the literary world.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text defines literary critics as the people whose job is to evaluate books.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
Home Console and Computer Games of the 1980s
Title | Approximate number of units sold worldwide | Genre | Developer
Super Mario Land | 18,140,000 | platformer | Nintendo R&D1
Baseball | 3,200,000 | sports | Nintendo R&D1
Tetris | 43,000,000 | puzzle | Nintendo R&D1
Kung Fu | 3,500,000 | action | Nintendo R&D1
A student is composing a paper about how the home video game industry grew across the globe during the 1980s. As part of this work, the student is examining how popular various genres of console and computer games were relative to one another. Drawing on the information in the table, the student observes that games in the genres of ______
option a: platformer and action sold nearly the same number of units.
option b: puzzle and sports sold nearly the same number of units.
option c: platformer and sports outsold the games in the other genres.
option d: puzzle and platformer outsold the games in the other genres.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Tetris (puzzle, 43,000,000) and Super Mario Land (platformer, 18,140,000) far outsold the sports and action titles.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
Effect of Various Soil Treatments on Mean Pineapple Fruit Weight and Size
Soil treatment | Weight (grams) | Length (centimeters) | Diameter (centimeters)
Control | 825.9 | 6.14 | 13.63
Biochar | 915.7 | 6.56 | 13.63
Compost | 864.8 | 6.15 | 13.22
Biochar and compost | 979.3 | 6.76 | 13.68
Biochar and NPK fertilizer | 1032.1 | 6.78 | 13.96
In Ghana, Emmanuel Hanyabui and his colleagues examined how different mixtures of soil additives affected pineapple growth. The additives tested included NPK fertilizer (a synthetic fertilizer supplying nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium), organic compost, and biochar (a carbon-dense material made from organic waste). According to the table, pineapple farmers lacking access to inorganic soil additives would most likely achieve the largest increase in fruit weight and size by applying ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Excluding inorganic additives, biochar and compost gives the greatest weight and size.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? A team of primate conservationists has recently launched a long-term investigation into how various conservation methods affect the Perrier's sifaka (Propithecus perrieri), a species whose population is presently estimated at roughly 500. Because these primates are so difficult to count precisely, however, researchers struggle to determine whether their numbers are rising, falling, or holding steady. As a result, the study may therefore ______
option a: risk making inaccurate conclusions about the effectiveness of different conservation strategies.
option b: cause other conservationists to adopt a new methodology for counting populations.
option c: benefit from including species beyond the Perrier's sifaka.
option d: fail to consider less-well-known conservation approaches for the Perrier's sifaka.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If the population can't be counted accurately, conclusions about strategy effectiveness may be wrong.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Across Puerto Rico, it's common for a city or town to be known by a nickname tied to one of its distinctive traits, such as its scenery, climate, celebrated residents, or main export. The municipality of Gurabo, for instance, is famous for the towering staircases that snake through the town ______ this distinction has earned it the fitting nickname of "the Town of the Stairs."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon correctly joins the two independent clauses.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? ______ a US state when it ratified the US Constitution on June 21, 1788, was thereby entitled, through its representatives to the US Congress, to vote on whether Alabama would be admitted as a state on December 14, 1819.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The participial phrase "having officially become..." modifies the subject without creating a run-on.

question:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
Operating at the almost inconceivably tiny scale of billionths of a meter, nanoengineers have discovered ways to harness graphene oxide ______ to boost the capacity of lithium-ion batteries.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The plural possessive "nanoparticles'" correctly shows properties belonging to multiple nanoparticles.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Resins carry out several important functions that keep conifers and many other kinds of trees healthy. ______ resins rapidly seal off wounds, which helps keep destructive insects and fungi from getting inside trees. These sticky substances also help trees hold on to the water they need to stay alive.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Sealing wounds is one illustration of the roles resins play, so "For example" fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? An artist's palette--the surface on which a painter arranges and blends colors--can offer valuable insight into that painter's creative process. In her 2024 book The Artist's Palette, Alexandra Loske examines the palettes of 50 different painters spanning 500 years. ______ Loske uncovers clues about the methods and practices of such artists as Kerry James Marshall, Artemisia Gentileschi, and Vincent van Gogh.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Analyzing the palettes is the very act through which Loske reveals the clues, so "In doing so" fits.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize the discovery of (20161) 1996 TR66 to an audience already familiar with Jane Luu?
Minor planets are astronomical objects that circle the Sun yet are classified as neither planets nor comets. Over her career, astronomer Jane Luu has discovered many minor planets. Together with colleagues David C. Jewitt, Jun Chen, and Chadwick Trujillo, she discovered the minor planet (20161) 1996 TR66 on October 8, 1996. Working with colleagues David C. Jewitt and Chadwick Trujillo, she discovered the minor planet (385201) 1999 RN215 on September 7, 1999.
option a: Astronomer Jane Luu helped discover not only the minor planet (20161) 1996 TR66 on October 8, 1996, but also (385201) 1999 RN215 on September 7, 1999.
option b: First there was the discovery of (20161) 1996 TR66 on October 8, 1996, and then on September 7, 1999, Jane Luu discovered yet another minor planet with the help of her colleagues David C. Jewitt and Chadwick Trujillo.
option c: Jane Luu is an astronomer famous for her discovery of many minor planets in our solar system, including (20161) 1996 TR66.
option d: On October 8, 1996, Jane Luu and her colleagues David C. Jewitt, Jun Chen, and Chadwick Trujillo made the exciting discovery of the minor planet (20161) 1996 TR66.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice D foregrounds the TR66 discovery for readers who already know Luu.

question:
The student wants to emphasize the combined deadweight tonnage of Panama's merchant ships in 2021. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
A merchant ship is any vessel hired to carry cargo or passengers. A ship's carrying capacity is also known as its deadweight tonnage (DWT). In 2021, a total of 7,980 merchant ships were registered in Panama. Together, these ships had a combined DWT of 344.2 million tons.
option a: In 2021, Panama had 7,980 merchant ships hired to carry cargo or passengers.
option b: There were a total of 7,980 merchant ships--ships hired to carry cargo or passengers--registered in Panama in 2021.
option c: The carrying capacity of a merchant ship is also known as deadweight tonnage.
option d: Combined, Panama's merchant ships had a deadweight tonnage of 344.2 million tons in 2021.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice D states the combined 344.2-million-ton deadweight tonnage.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize Edison's reliance on Upton?
Thomas Edison is considered one of the most significant inventors in US history. Having had little formal schooling, Edison depended on specialist employees at his various laboratories and offices to carry out the technical work behind many of his inventions. Francis Robbins Upton, a mathematician and physicist, worked at the Menlo Park laboratory and is best known for inventing the electric fire alarm. John Kruesi, a machinist, worked at Edison Machine Works and is best known for directing the installation of underground electricity distribution cables for the Edison Electric Tube Company.
option a: Francis Robbins Upton, a mathematician and physicist, was known for his valuable contribution to the field of technology.
option b: Having received little formal education, Thomas Edison depended on specialized employees, including mathematician and physicist Francis Robbins Upton, for many of his inventions.
option c: Francis Robbins Upton, a mathematician and physicist, worked at the Menlo Park laboratory.
option d: Most of Thomas Edison's employees had successful careers independent of working for him; for example, Francis Robbins Upton, who worked at the Menlo Park laboratory, was an accomplished mathematician and physicist.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B directly ties Edison's dependence on specialists to Upton.

question:
The student wants to place the 1821 Declaration of Independence in the context of Valle's changing political beliefs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
On September 15, 1821, leaders of the Province of Guatemala proclaimed Central America's independence from the Spanish Empire. The accompanying Declaration of Independence was written by José Cecilio del Valle, a Honduran scholar and politician. Although the 1812 Spanish Constitution had granted Central America a measure of independence, the Spanish king repealed it in 1814. Valle, a loyal advisor to the Spanish Empire's administrators in Central America, had long opposed independence. His view shifted after Colonel Rafael del Riego's 1820 revolt, which demanded the restoration of rights lost in 1814.
option a: Long an opponent of Central American independence, Valle changed his mind after an 1820 revolt and wrote the 1821 declaration.
option b: A change in Valle's political beliefs that occurred when the Spanish king repealed the 1812 constitution led to Valle writing Central America's Declaration of Independence.
option c: Colonel Riego's revolt was the inspiration that Valle, a long-standing opponent of Central American independence, needed to change his political beliefs.
option d: The writing of Central America's Declaration of Independence may not have happened were it not for Colonel Riego's 1820 revolt.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A frames the 1821 declaration against Valle's shift from opposing to supporting independence.

question:
Which choice best states the main purpose of the text? The passage below is from Robert Lowell's 1964 poem "For the Union Dead." The South Boston Aquarium closed permanently in 1954.
The old South Boston Aquarium now sits in a Sahara of snow. Boards cover its shattered windows. The bronze cod weathervane has lost half its scales. The once-airy tanks stand dry.
option a: To describe details of the deteriorated state of a building
option b: To contrast the effects of different kinds of weather on a building
option c: To argue that a building should be rehabilitated
option d: To explain why a once-popular building was abandoned
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text catalogs the aquarium's decay, so its purpose is to describe a building's deteriorated state.

Scientists gathered information about brown bears in Katmai National Park in Alaska, recording each bear's sex, age, and approximate weight. According to the table, the bear with the highest approximate weight was the one with identification number ______

question:
The student wants to emphasize a difference between Beaux and Artschwager. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
The Carnegie Prize is an international art competition run by the Carnegie Museum of Art in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. In 1899, US painter Cecilia Beaux won a Carnegie Prize gold medal for a painting titled Mother and Daughter. In 1995, US sculptor Richard Artschwager won a Carnegie Prize gold medal for a sculpture titled Table Prepared in the Presence of Enemies.
option a: Beaux won a Carnegie Prize gold medal for a painting, while Artschwager won for a sculpture.
option b: Carnegie Prize gold medals have been awarded to both painters and sculptors.
option c: Both Beaux and Artschwager won Carnegie Prize gold medals for their artworks.
option d: Beaux won a Carnegie Prize gold medal in 1899 for the painting Mother and Daughter.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A contrasts Beaux's painting with Artschwager's sculpture.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to introduce Acoustic Soul to an audience already familiar with India Arie? India Arie is an African American singer and songwriter. The media outlet BBC Music has described her music as a "blend of hip hop, soul and folk [that is] as subtle as it [is] inspired." Her first studio album, Acoustic Soul, was released in 2001. It features the song "Promises." Nioka Workman played cello on the album.
option a: "Promises," a song by singer and songwriter India Arie, is featured on the album Acoustic Soul.
option b: Nioka Workman played cello on singer and songwriter India Arie's 2001 album, Acoustic Soul.
option c: Featuring the song "Promises," Acoustic Soul is India Arie's first studio album.
option d: India Arie's music has been described as a "blend of hip hop, soul and folk [that is] as subtle as it [is] inspired."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice C introduces Acoustic Soul as Arie's debut album for readers who already know her.

question:
As it is used in the text, what does the word "traces" most nearly mean? The passage below is adapted from John Matheus's 1925 short story "Fog."
The fog stretched its tentacles across the city and the river, little by little wiping out traces of the familiar scenery. By five-thirty the old Panhandle bridge, held up by massive sandstone pillars, still sturdy just as it had been when built fifty years earlier for a generation now gone behind the portals of life, had become a ghostly outline against the sky.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The fog erases the visible signs of the landscape, so "traces" means indications.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Science fiction has long acted as a ______ real-world technological progress. In fact, from Jules Verne's 1865 novel From the Earth to the Moon prompting advances in aerospace engineering to the television show Star Trek inspiring the design of the forerunner of today's smartphones, such stories have driven many genuine innovations.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Science fiction spurs real innovations, so it acts as a catalyst of technological advancement.
